t0_note: t0, the start of the descent sequence (the pilot parachute's firing), from the Huygens key events table (PDS Atmospheres Node); every offset below is in seconds from it. Entry interface, the descent altitudes and the landing come from the probe's own track (data/huygens.json: DTWG reconstruction), not from this file.

facts.text: Reconstructed times of the descent from t0 = 2005-014T09:10:20.828 UTC: pilot chute inflates +1.4 s, back cover released and main chute deployed +2.5 s, main chute inflated +4.9 s, heat shield separation +32.5 s, data transmission begins +143.6 s, main chute released and stabilizer deployed +900 s (111 km), surface lamp on +8745 s, surface impact +8870 s (11:38:10.8 UTC), end of the Cassini-probe link +13203 s (12:50:23.8 UTC), last signal detected by Earth-based radio telescopes +20559 s.

The pilot parachute is 2.6 m across, the main parachute 8.3 m; after about 15 minutes the main chute is released and a 3 m drogue carries the probe the rest of the way. Huygens reaches Titan's air at 1,270 km.
Cassini stops collecting data once the landing site drops below Titan's horizon, then turns its high-gain antenna to Earth and sends the data, several copies of it.

Huygens was known to be alive at 11:25 CET (10:25 UTC) when the Green Bank radio telescope picked up its faint carrier directly; the first science data reached ESOC in Darmstadt at 17:19 CET (16:19 UTC).
Cassini never listened to the probe's channel A because of a missing command, so only about 350 of the 700 planned pictures came back, and the Doppler wind measurement was lost.
The temperature at the landing site was 93.8 K (-179 C); the probe landed among rounded pebbles of water ice.
